title: Army Reserve Career Counselor (Army Reserve)

10-79V. MOS 79V--Army Reserve Career Counselor (Army Reserve), CMF 79
    a. Major Duties. Transfers, counsels, informs, and retains qualified Soldiers in the Individual
Ready Reserve (IRR), Troop Program Unit (TPU), Active Guard and Reserve (AGR), and
Individual Mobilization Augmentee (IMA) programs to continue service and professional growth in
the U.S. Army Reserve (USAR). Supports USAR end strength objectives by retaining qualified
Soldiers and filling critical vacancies. Prospects units for qualified applicants for officer
commissioning programs and AGR CMF 79 accessions. Supports USAR units in executing the
U.S Army Reserve Retention Program and Chief, Army Reserve (CAR) policies.
       (1) MOSC 79V2O (Personnel only). Soldiers assessed in MOS 79V (Army Reserve Career
Counselor) prior to promotion to SSG.
       (2) MOSC 79V3O (Personnel only). Soldiers assessed in MOS 79V (Army Reserve Career
Counselor) prior to promotion to SFC.
       (3) MOSC 79V4O. Determines eligibility for transfer, reenlistment or extension, and officer
accessioning programs. Updates records contained in the Retention Management Software
(RMS) as well as applicable personnel systems. Conducts multiple methods of contacting IRR,
TPU, and IMA Soldiers. Pre-qualifies and counsels to determine military and civilian status.
Schedules appointments and conducts sales interviews to obtain transfers to the selected reserve
(SELRES) and retention interviews to gain reenlistments and extensions. Updates personnel
records contained in RMS through unit personnel or Total Army Personnel Database – Reserve
(TAPDB -R). Counsels IRR and TPU Soldiers on enlistment contracts, service obligations,
incentives, and benefits of Army Reserve participation. Executes documents to complete IRR to
SELRES transfer, reenlistment, extension, and developmental counseling forms in accordance
with applicable United States Army Reserve Careers Group (ARCG), USAR and U.S. Army
regulations, pamphlets, and policies. Prepares and conducts unit presentations on personal and
professional development, Army Reserve features and benefits, employment opportunities, officer
commissioning programs, retention topics, and the Selected Reserve Incentive Program (SRIP)
policy. Executes the HRC Personnel Accountability Muster Program in efforts to ready the IRR
population in support of U.S. Army missions. Establishes and maintains a partnership with
multiple assigned units and assists command teams in executing the Army Reserve Retention
Program. Assist unit leaders in all matters pertaining retention by providing guidance, support,
and recommendations for development of unit incentive award programs. Attends multiple unit
training assemblies (MUTA) for unit(s) supported. Conduct interviews with Soldiers, Family
members, and unit leadership to address the effectiveness of current unit policies and unit
training on the unit retention program. Provide recommendations to the unit leadership for
improvement. Maintain regular contact with unit members to help prevent and solve individual
problems, discuss issues, provide information, answer questions, and recover unsatisfactory
participants. Provide retention trends and recommendations to unit leadership. Trains unit
personal as Duty Appointed Reenlistment NCO (DARN). Provide unit leadership information and
training attrition personnel and on all administrative requirements necessary to retain Soldiers.
Provide leadership with feedback as required after each unit Battle Assembly and Annual
Training mission to keep the unit leadership informed of the unit retention program. Assist unit
with recommendations and options for transfer, separation, and discharge requests. Assist in the
development of the Unit Sponsorship Program. Complete expiration term of service (ETS)
counseling. Work directly with unit administrative personnel to support/complete retention issues.
Establish and maintain relationships with agencies outside of the United States Army Reserve. to
assist the total Army end-strength.
    (4) MOSC 79V5O. Performs duties shown in preceding skill levels and provides technical
guidance as required. Establishes performance standards, monitors, and evaluates subordinates
on their overall effectiveness to include their leadership capabilities while managing and
mentoring their subordinate ARCCs. Evaluates retention activities/programs (e.g. presentations
and briefings, qualification interviews and techniques, reenlistment packets) for assigned area of
responsibility. Counsels, develops, motivates, and rates ARCCs assigned IAW AR 623-3 and
locally established policy. Conducts monthly performance counseling with each assigned ARCCs.
Responsible for establishing and implementing a written yearly training program designed to
address the specific training needs and levels of experience of assigned ARCCs. Provide ARCCs
with market data, trends, and other pertinent demographic information. Works with senior unit
 leaders to ensure awareness of and compliance to the Army Reserve Retention Program, CAR
policies, and ARCG guidance. Advise JAG and IG on inquires related to Army Reserve retention.
Discusses and plans activities to meet strength missions and conducts Army Reserve retention
training, presentations and briefings as required. Assists in the hiring of new ARCCs as directed
by the Battalion. Constantly scan assigned units for qualified Soldiers for active, guard, and
reserve (AGR) program, officer commissioning programs, and professional growth opportunities.
Assess the effectiveness of area retention, attrition management and retention incentive/awards
programs and make recommendations for improvement. Provides administrative guidance and
technical support to assigned ARCCs. Monitors assigned ARCCs to ensure compliance with
applicable regulatory guidance. Assign and assist in the training of unit DARN personnel. Advises
the Battalion leadership concerning mission accomplishment, personnel, operations, and training.
Assists in developing, maintaining, and analyzing statistical data of assigned area demographics,
as well as unit losses, unit climate information and personnel data to form current and projected
trends. Provides sustainment and remedial training for assigned ARCCs as needed to maintain
skills and prevent poor performance. Verifies all applicable updates, documents, transactions,
and actions are completed and correct in RMS. Ensure RMS data correctly portrays the work
completed.
    (5) MOSC 79V60, Serves as the senior enlisted subject matter expert (SME) for retention and
transition and advises commander at all levels concerning retention. Coordinates and employs
strategic plans for mission success including mission and operational market analysis, and
historical trends. Manages enlisted Soldiers through the talent management process of hiring,
assignments, and transfers. Continuously monitors and assesses organizational training, makes
recommendations, and evaluates training outcomes through measures of performance and
measures of effectiveness. Oversees the Noncommissioned Officer Development Program
(NCODP). Enforces standards, discipline, and assesses morale. Supervises headquarters staff
personnel and provides counsel to the operations team and executive officer. Conducts area
quality assurance visits. Fosters relationships and liaisons with command leadership of troop
program units (TPUs), regional support commands (RSCs), major supporting commands (MSCs),
Soldier readiness processing centers (SRPCs), Reserve Components Career Counselors
(RCCCs), and United States Army Recruiting Command (USAREC) personnel
     b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. The Army Reserve
Career Counselor must possess the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A physical profile of 232321.
         (3) Hold the rank/grade of SGT/E5, SSG/E6 or SFC/E7 (Non-waiverable).
         (4) Qualifying scores.
              (a) A minimum score of 100 in aptitude area GT (Non-waiverable).
              (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power
Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
         (5) Must possess ALC for SGT-SSG (Non-waiverable).
         (6) Must be a high school graduate or GED equivalent (Non-waiverable).
         (7) A security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to maintain the
MOS. Waiverable for transfer to 79V position, and/or attendance at the 79V course, with a
favorable ENTNAC/NACI/NAC or NACLC. Must obtain secret security clearance and automated
system access prior to award of MOS 79V. Failure to obtain or maintain systems access will
result in reclassification to another MOS consistent with the needs of the Army.
         (8) Must possess a valid state motor vehicle operator license (Non-waiverable).
         (9) Must be assigned to a valid position to attend MOS training.
         (10) Must have more than 8 years total military service.
         (11) Be recommended by a LTC or higher commander. Additionally, all applicants for
PMOS 79V must be interviewed and endorsed by a current Army Reserve Careers Group
Battalion Sergeant Major (SGM).
         (12) Formal training: Successful completion of the MOS 79V Army Reserve Career
Counselor Course conducted at the Army Reserve Readiness Training Center (ARRTC) under
the auspices of the Recruiting and Retention College (RRC) is mandatory. MOS 79V may be
 awarded to Soldiers in the rank of SGT-SFC who complete MOS qualification training and are
assigned to a valid 79V position (Non-waiverable).
          (13) Army Reserve Career Counselor is the entry level for all Soldiers reclassifying to
79V. All reclassifying Soldiers must be assigned to an Army Reserve Career Counselor position
within the ARCG table of distribution and allowance (TDA). Soldiers must successfully serve 24
months in the ARCC position prior to assignment to developmental, operational, or broadening
assignment in or outside of the ARCG TDA.
          (14) Waiver authority is Army Reserve Careers Group (ARCG), Operations Branch, 85
Chamberlin Street, Building 6579, Fort Knox, KY, 40121-5107. ARCG is the proponent for the
MOS 79V. All reclassification requests and waivers must be e-mailed to the Senior Career
Management NCO / Proponent at usarmy.usarc.arcg.mbx.79v-personnel-development-
division@army.mil.
  c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated
with all MOS)).
    4R--Reserve Component Career Counselor (Effective 202512).
   d. Physical requirements and standards of grade (SG). Physical requirements and SG relating
to MOS 79V are listed in the following tables:
      (1) Table 10-79V-1. Physical requirements.
      (2) Table 10-79V-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE (N/A).
      (3) Table 10-79V-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
